features.physical: names a physical event with mass and direction (the house rule: physical metaphors only)
features.sequence: signals a fixed, specified series of steps
features.obligation: reads as an assignment: you need to do this
features.shelf: echoes the wellness shelf, where this word is sold as a feeling
features.clinical: reads as medical or institutional, done to a patient
features.costume: claims a formality or precision the sentence does not carry
features.discreet: gives nothing away to somebody glancing at the screen
features.fit: reads as the sentence it replaces, without a rewrite
features.truth: still says exactly what the engine does (pass one, which beats every other)

strings.why: The primary action on Summary and on Story. Nothing beside the button says what the sequence is.
Eyebrow over the heaviest address on Summary. The P form has no verb to carry the imperative, so it reads as if the address were the protocol's name.

strings.R: Run a release here. Four channels, twenty five lines.
strings.P: Run the protocol here. Four channels, twenty five lines.
strings.why: The address card button. The line beside it states the sequence, so "protocol" is earned here: it names a thing that is exactly specified.

strings.R: Nothing is held here, so there is nothing to release. A release opens once this address is carrying.
strings.P: Nothing is held here, so there is nothing for the protocol to run on. The protocol opens once this address is carrying.
strings.why: Ships today with both words in one refusal. Protocol has no verb, so "nothing to release" has to be rebuilt.
Menus are one word, and the word says what the control does. A noun cannot be that word.

The eyebrow on the card a run ends on, above "0 cleared entirely, 66 weight freed" for James. "Released" states a body event the instrument did not observe. "Protocol complete" states only what the software knows.

strings.R: Release empties the address. The coherent opposite is installing on the same pass.
strings.P: The protocol empties the address. The coherent opposite is installing on the same pass.
strings.why: The mechanism in one line. Release is mechanic one of two; the protocol is both. Swapping the word makes the protocol do half of itself.

strings.R: Release has about 1.2 points left to give you. The laws hold expression down from here.
strings.P: The protocol has about 1.2 points left to give you. The laws hold expression down from here.
strings.why: The headroom is a property of discharge on the shadow. A protocol does not run out; what it can still discharge does.

strings.R: Nothing released on a worked example.
strings.P: No protocol runs on a worked example.
strings.why: The run on a worked example does walk every line to the end, and then refuses to write. "No protocol runs" is false. "Nothing released" is exact.

strings.R: Release. The discharge of stored charge through the nervous system. Physical and observable: heat, shaking, tears, breath shifts. The pattern loses its power source.
strings.P: Protocol. The sequence that discharges stored charge through the nervous system. Physical and observable: heat, shaking, tears, breath shifts. The pattern loses its power source.
strings.why: A protocol cannot be a discharge, so the definition has to change its subject, and "physical and observable" then describes a list of steps.

strings.R: The release is complete when the body settles. Breath deepens. Vision may clear. That is the signal.
strings.P: The protocol is complete when the body settles. Breath deepens. Vision may clear. That is the signal.
strings.why: The end condition is bodily. The shipped protocol ends after its lines whatever the body does, so the P form promises a stop rule the product does not have.

strings.R: Ten patterns a week, for life. Two releases at one address, and unlimited rerunning of anything already open.
strings.P: Ten patterns a week, for life. Two protocols at one address, and unlimited rerunning of anything already open.
strings.why: Paywall copy. "Two protocols at one address" reads as two different regimens, and a regimen sold by the week reads as a prescription.

people.says: I hold the room for everyone. I have not been held in four years and I would not know how to ask.

src.physical: Her trade is the body; release is a word she uses with clients in its physical sense.
src.sequence: "Tell me what to run and how long it takes." (RESEARCH-icp.md, section 4)
src.obligation: "I hold the room for everyone." She is already carrying every obligation in the room.
src.shelf: Knows the shelf, uses the word professionally anyway, so the echo costs little.
src.clinical: "A map I could put in front of a client." Client facing wording has to hold up.
src.costume: "Said back to me by something with no stake in being kind to me." Dressing up is a stake.
src.fit: Reads at eleven at night, on a phone, in bed.
src.truth: She will repeat it to a client. It has to be true.

people.says: I work until the work is done and the work is never done. Rest feels like a moral failure.

src.physical: Wants a cost, not a sensation.
src.sequence: "What does it actually do at nine on a Tuesday." A thing with steps can be scheduled.
src.obligation: "Does it give me back an hour or does it give me another practice to fail at." Rest already reads to her as a moral failure; an assignment lands on that.
src.costume: Wants the P and L, not the packaging.

people.says: I can see what is wrong with anything in four seconds. It has cost me two studios.

src.physical: "Does it show me the mechanism. I need the schematic." A mechanism is a physical verb.
src.sequence: Accepts a sequence where it is stated.
src.obligation: "Help is the wrong verb and the fact that you used it tells me who you think I am."
src.shelf: Reads wellness in four seconds and closes the tab.
src.clinical: Borrowed clinical authority is the same move as borrowed nerve names.
src.costume: "That is precision as costume." (RESEARCH-icp.md, section 5, the sharpest break in the study)
src.fit: Sees a rebuilt sentence in four seconds.
src.truth: "Give me a claim specific enough to be wrong."

people.says: Everything happens for a reason. I have said that at three funerals and I believed it each time.

src.physical: "None of them told me where it lives." She wants it in the body.
src.sequence: The voice skill's pass 7: "Does she stay on the screen or decide this is homework."
src.obligation: Walked at a single word once: "It told me I am incoherent. I closed it." A word that assigns her something is the same shape as a word that grades her.
src.shelf: The only one of the six for whom the familiar word is trust rather than a smell. Six modalities all said release.
src.clinical: "A moral adjective delivered by software to a person in crisis is a verdict." Clinical distance reads to her as being processed.
src.discreet: "This is the one I would screenshot for the group chat." She wants to be seen.
src.truth: Weighs truth, less than the others: "I expect it to see me."

people.says: Pain is information. I have raced on a stress fracture. I would do it again.

src.physical: "Pain is information." Heat and shaking are data to him.
src.sequence: "Name the one thing capping my output and where it sits. I will train it like anything else." A training protocol is his native unit.
src.obligation: Wants to be handed the set. An assignment is the product.
src.shelf: "If my resting rate does not move and my last kilometre does not move, this is a mood."
src.clinical: Sports medicine language reads as seriousness.
src.costume: Does the arithmetic; catches a claim with nothing under it.
src.fit: "Put it in text and I will read it in nine seconds."
src.truth: Checks the numbers, not the nouns.

people.says: I make the call and I sleep fine. People find that cold. It is what they hired.

src.sequence: "Front load the finding." Operational language is his.
src.obligation: "Help implies a deficit. Ask me instead what it improves." Being put on a protocol is being a patient.
src.shelf: Level 3, defended. A wellness word ends it.
src.clinical: Protocol is what he writes for other people, not what he is put on.
src.costume: "You moved between them without telling me." He audits the join.
src.discreet: "I will not open that on a plane, or in my office with the door open." (DD panel)
